strengths: The paper addresses an important NLP problem: selecting an effective teacher size under limited distillation resources. A reliable teacher-selection rule would have practical value.

The GPT-2 and Pythia sweeps provide evidence that larger teachers can produce worse students under the studied protocol. Connecting these experiments to a 3B bilingual model makes the investigation practically grounded.

MiniMA achieves competitive results against many evaluated 3B models. Table 4 reports improvements over training without distillation on all six benchmarks, including GSM8K increasing from 5.08 to 8.11. These results support the usefulness of the particular training recipe.

The paper provides pruning and loss formulations, dataset-mixture statistics, substantial training details, evaluation protocols, and repository/model links. Evaluation spans language modeling, knowledge, reasoning, coding, and instruction following.
weaknesses: The central law T ≈ 2.5S is insufficiently established. Students are pruned from their respective teachers, so teacher size changes student architecture, inherited initialization, and pruning severity together. Consequently, the experiments cannot separate a general capacity-gap relationship from properties of this pruning-and-recovery procedure. The manuscript also does not adequately explain how Figure 2's optimal-teacher points are obtained from the discrete experimental grid, or report fitting uncertainty, residuals, or validation on held-out teacher–student pairs.

The claimed generalization across settings exceeds the evidence. Appendix B compares approximately 90% and 100% checkpoints of the same training runs; this provides little evidence of invariance across substantially different data budgets. The LLaMA experiment changes the pruning procedure and compares only 7B versus 13B teachers for one 3B student size. This supports a particular comparison, but does not locate an optimum or validate the predicted scaling relationship. Whether the 13B teacher receives equivalent bilingual adaptation is also unclear.

The compute-efficiency claim needs materially corrected accounting. Table 7 reports approximately 4.0 × 10^9 TFLOPs for MiniMA's distillation but omits the teacher's additional 126B-token adaptation in Appendix C. Using the paper's own 6ND approximation, adaptation adds approximately 5.3 × 10^9 TFLOPs, bringing the total to approximately 9.3 × 10^9 before pruning costs, even treating original teacher pretraining as a sunk cost. Competitor estimates also depend on explicitly rumored GPT-4 architecture and Mistral training quantities. The claimed Pareto frontier needs recomputation and sensitivity analysis.

The 'impossible triangle' is presented more strongly than justified. Reporting additional resource requirements for two existing approaches does not establish that every method improving distillation across a large capacity gap must incur such costs. Likewise, one MiniMA operating point cannot establish superior performance at any compute budget. These statements should be framed as scoped empirical observations.

The instruction-following evaluation has unresolved reliability and reproducibility limitations. The GPT-4 version, response-order controls, and decoding settings are not adequately specified. Human evaluation omits the number of annotators and comparisons, agreement statistics, and uncertainty around Elo rankings. Appendix M's Spearman correlation of 0.54 is not equivalent to 54% agreement. Appendix K acknowledges possible benchmark contamination without resolving it, limiting interpretation of the fine-tuning gains.

Several interpretations require correction: Table 9 compares token perplexities across different vocabularies, which cannot directly establish relative language-model quality; Table 15 praises a coding solution that incorrectly returns the first array when the second array is empty. More broadly, the useful implementation and conditional observations could support a revised contribution, but the central scaling-law validation and compute analysis require substantive revision before a sound Findings recommendation.
